Headline: Drought Tightens Its Hold Across the U.S
This map shows drought conditions across the United States in late October 2024, with areas ranging from "Abnormally Dry" to "Exceptional Drought." The worst impacts are in the Southwest, like Texas and New Mexico, and parts of the Midwest, such as Kansas and Nebraska, while the Northeast and coastal areas are less affected. I wonder what is causing all these droughts. Is this a result of climate change? Why is a place like West Virginia so much drier than Virginia, which is right next to it? This relates to me and my community because in the past months, we have been experiencing little to no rainfall. The drought caused multiple, small, but dangerous wildfires, even one just over a mile from my house. These droughts are damaging places around me and it's very concerning.
